problem: Existing embodied navigation/3D-VLM approaches produce incoherent, unstable reasoning traces that generalize poorly, and struggle to balance long-horizon semantic reasoning with low-latency reactive control.
motivation: Embodied agents need to jointly reason, plan, converse and navigate in real time on resource-limited robots. Directly applying R1-style RL to 3D VLMs is unstable, and slow deliberate reasoning conflicts with real-time control, motivating a CoT cold start, multi-reward RL and a dual-system design.
key_idea: Cold-start a 3D VLM on a 110K synthetic navigation CoT dataset, refine it with GRPO using format, understanding and navigation rewards, and split inference into a slow semantic reasoner and a fast reactive controller (Fast-in-Slow).
insight: The ablations show every component contributes: the dual system beats slow-only (SR 61.2) and fast-only (SR 58.7) on R2R-CE (72.5), and each reward helps on HM3D-OVON (SR 34.5 with no rewards to 42.2 with all three, with pairwise combinations in between). The KL coefficient β=0.02 is a sweet spot on RxR-CE. Caveat: dialogue/reasoning/planning stay on par with the 3D-R1 initialization rather than improving, so gains are concentrated in navigation.
method: Nav-CoT-110K data engine: prompts Gemini 2.5 Pro with instruction, history and current egocentric views, action options and a format spec to generate <think>/<action> CoT (~115K raw), filtered by rule-based checks and action-vs-GT-path verification to 110K; instructions from R2R, R2R-CE, RxR-CE, SOON and HM3D-OVON.
Cold-start SFT: initialize from 3D-R1 and fine-tune on Nav-CoT-110K for 2 epochs (batch 8, AdamW, cosine LR 1e-4 to 1e-5) to learn structured think-then-act outputs.

GRPO RL with three rewards: format (binary template adherence), understanding (exact answer match + CLIPScore of image and answer), navigation (exp(-k·DF(T,T̂)) path reward + exp(-k‖p̂-p‖) endpoint reward); group-normalized advantages, clipped objective, KL β=0.02 to the SFT policy.

Fast-in-Slow reasoning: the slow System 2 aggregates visual history into latent features h_t; the fast System 1 reuses the final transformer blocks and fuses RGB, depth and point-cloud tokens with h_t to predict a short-horizon action sequence.
Asynchronous coordination: slow:fast update ratio 1:n with n≈3, so one slow update guides n consecutive fast steps.
Parameter-efficient tuning: LoRA (rank 6, α 8) on the last 8 blocks, ~12M LoRA params, ~142M trainable in total (~98% fewer than full fine-tuning).
Real-world deployment: cloud inference on a server, with the WHEELTEC R550 (Jetson Orin Nano) streaming egocentric RGB over WiFi 6E and an STM32 converting commands to motor PWM.

setting.backbone: 3D-R1 (3D VLM) initialized, SFT + GRPO fine-tuned with LoRA, Fast-in-Slow dual system
setting.model_size: not stated (~142M trainable parameters, ~12M of them LoRA)
setting.training_data: Nav-CoT-110K (Gemini 2.5 Pro synthesized CoT from R2R, R2R-CE, RxR-CE, SOON, HM3D-OVON instructions) for SFT, then RL on benchmark tasks with GT answers/trajectories
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + scene point cloud tokens + language instruction, with history frames
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions: move forward 25 cm, turn left/right 30°, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE / HM3D); real world with WHEELTEC R550
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT trajectories/endpoints used only in RL rewards)

numbers.extra: uses single RGB + depth, no panorama, no odometry, no waypoint predictor
split not specified in the paper
split not specified; reported as embodied reasoning with language metrics

numbers_note: Real-world results (Table V: NE/SR in meeting room, lounge, corridor) are not included; the SR values are printed above 1 (e.g. 1.03, 1.12), which looks inconsistent. Latency of ~95 ms on the server is in Table VI. Ablation variants (Slow-only, Fast-only) are in Tables VII-IX.
results: Nav-R1 reaches SR 72.5 / SPL 68.8 on R2R-CE val-unseen and SR 71.3 / SPL 66.3 on RxR-CE, above the strongest baseline CorrectNav (65.1/62.3 and 69.3/63.3). On HM3D-OVON it beats MTU3D (val-unseen SR 42.2 vs 40.8, SPL 20.1 vs 12.1). Dialogue, planning and reasoning are roughly on par with 3D-R1.
limitations: Nav-CoT-110K is synthesized from existing benchmarks and may not capture real-world complexity; only RGB-D and language are used.
Deployment relies on cloud inference, limiting edge scalability; server latency (~95 ms) is slightly higher than NaVid/Uni-NaVid.
No gains over the 3D-R1 base on dialogue, planning and reasoning tasks; the paper does not disentangle the effect of SFT vs RL data on the navigation gains.
